name: update-partition-coexistence
description: The argument for a partition that runs components below its own level — the partition's own memory-mixing argument, beside the task's execution-time one. AUTOSAR advises against sharing an OS-Application across safety integrity levels, and ISO 26262-9's coexistence clause permits the argument; the model takes free text and grades none of it, so SWCraft can report that mixing exists and never that it is handled.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model with `PARTITION0` rated B on the unrated `CORE0` and no argument. `Task_10ms` runs `ExampleConsumerSWC`, which derives `QM`, so the baseline already carries one `safety.component-below-partition` finding. The change set writes the argument.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the address exactly. The direction lives in the VALUE — `""` to a text is the weakening, a text back to `""` makes the check refuse again — and the guard decides it by comparing two models. `declare_partition_coexistence` is the safety act, answered once for the whole change set, which is why the status is `committed`.

input.intent: Record the memory-mixing argument for PARTITION0.

operations.value: The partition's components are placed in separate memory regions under memory protection; the argument is recorded in the item's safety case.

delta.after: The partition's components are placed in separate memory regions under memory protection; the argument is recorded in the item's safety case.

expected.notes: `committed`, for the reason `update-task-coexistence.json` is: writing the argument makes `safety.component-below-partition` stop refusing, so the host answered a second, independent question, and the question names the PARTITION — a kind of its own, so a task's prompt did not move. What the accepted result records is that an argument EXISTS, never that interference is prevented.
